name: Chocolate / cocoa
description: Cocoa in all its forms — and a major histamine offender.

tcm.note: Not classical; modern sources call it warming-damp.

histamine.note: Tyramine and phenylethylamine rather than histamine. Theobromine does inhibit DAO, but SIGHI marks that on energy drinks, not on cocoa.

nutrition.highlight: theobromine, not caffeine, is the lift

stimulant.note: Mostly theobromine with a little caffeine. Theobromine is a far weaker stimulant and clears more slowly — which is why chocolate never feels like coffee.

guna.note: Stimulating, which is the definition of rajasic rather than a judgement on it.

effects.note: A 35g dark chocolate bar improved verbal memory two hours later compared with a calorie-matched white chocolate bar in a trial of ninety-eight young adults, though results for attention and response inhibition specifically are more mixed and appear to depend on how much cocoa the chocolate actually contains. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.

Two small trials of dark chocolate at 70-85% cocoa — a bar-sized serving eaten daily for several weeks — found reduced negative mood in healthy adults and reduced depression scores in menopausal women, tracking with changes in gut bacteria rather than the popular but weak serotonin or 'love chemical' story often told about chocolate. Milk and lower-cocoa chocolate were the comparison in these trials and showed no such effect. A possible effect, not a promise — response to it varies from person to person.
